catalogue.snapshot: Fresh on-disk registry; release art is still mutable.

usage: Visual reference and attribution only. No publisher code, art, character, logo or audio is copied into production.

acceptedDirection.status: User accepted this aspirational 3D art direction for all games, as relayed by root.
acceptedDirection.application: Use the family references to translate the accepted direction into each game’s actual playfield and controls.
acceptedDirection.scope: The concept is an art target. Runtime appearance, materials, lighting, assets and interactions require separate implementation and native verification.

verificationScope: Official source HTML/presskit/store provenance and live image endpoint status/type verified. No new browser tabs or remote media files downloaded. Image pixels were not independently inspected in this metadata pass; root must inspect the rendered moodboard. Lessons are proposed design interpretations, not claims of feature parity or approved final art.

references.title: 51 Worldwide Games / Clubhouse Games
visualLessons: Study board and piece materials together: one coherent light direction, readable silhouettes and a quieter surrounding table.
Use the actual board as the main identity; reduce equal-weight pill cards and keep turn information compact.

references.title: BATTLESHIP
visualLessons: Study separation of personal harbor, target chart and firing action.
Make ships recognizable silhouettes while keeping hit, miss and coordinate marks readable at phone scale.

references.title: Drawful Animate
visualLessons: Treat the drawing as a framed exhibit and make surrounding character art secondary.
Use expressive hand-made identity in the frame and tools; keep the canvas surface clean enough to judge strokes.

references.title: Codenames App
visualLessons: Study large word labels and consistent card geometry before adding ornamental texture.
Use a clear visual relationship between clue, current task and candidate words; give feedback its own stable area.

references.title: Quiplash 3
visualLessons: Give the prompt and competing answers the stage; place players and round metadata at the edges.
Build one distinctive authored frame and character language rather than many interchangeable dashboard cards.

references.title: The Poll Mine
visualLessons: Study how choices and group results can become a scene with a clear reading order.
Keep choice labels immediately readable; reveal vote distribution as a separate, deliberate beat.

references.title: WarioWare: Get It Together!
visualLessons: Give each short task a distinct illustrated setup, one imperative and an obvious target.
Reserve motion and exaggerated scale for the action; keep persistent score and timer decoration small.

references.title: Puyo Puyo Tetris 2
visualLessons: Study strong orb silhouettes, distinct owner colors and a contained playfield.
Keep a chain readable through successive stages; effects should resolve back to an unambiguous settled state.

references.title: Mario Kart 8 Deluxe
visualLessons: Judge camera height, horizon and track-edge readability together so the next driving choice is visible.
Use a recognizable vehicle, pickup and obstacle silhouette language; make speed and item feedback brief and spatial.

references.title: Tricky Towers
visualLessons: Study how separate player towers read as distinct silhouettes against a simple scene.
Keep block shapes legible at distance and give failure or collapse a short, readable motion sequence.

references.title: Besiege
visualLessons: Use as a comparison for medieval construction materials, block edges and a clean silhouette in a 3D environment.
Let visible construction and impact locations explain destruction; target feedback must remain readable through debris.

references.title: Heads Up!
visualLessons: Study a performance prompt that reads instantly across a room.
Give the performer a single clear instruction and a compact phase cue; preserve the social action as the main event.

references.title: Zoom gallery on iPad
visualLessons: Use solely as a video-layout analogy: preserve usable faces and stable participant labels.
Plan a large current performer or target area and a restrained participant strip before adding prompt and voting overlays.

families.label: Board tabletop
families.direction: A crafted physical board on a quiet table, compact game title and turn rail, restrained secondary controls.

families.label: Tactical chart
families.direction: A readable harbor and target chart with deliberate placement, aiming and firing states.

families.label: Drawing studio
families.direction: A generous clean canvas, authored tools and a gallery-like reveal; art belongs around the drawing.

families.label: Semantic and word
families.direction: Large words or tiles, a stable input area and feedback that can be scanned as a ranked list or sequence.

families.label: Social and voting
families.direction: One large prompt or answer duel in an illustrated stage, with a distinct private-entry and public-reveal rhythm.

families.label: Speed arcade
families.direction: One clear action per screen, a distinct task illustration, quick feedback and a calm timer/score edge.

families.label: Chain arcade
families.direction: A crisp cell grid with readable orb ownership and bounded bursts that end in a stable board.

families.label: Kart 3D
families.direction: A confident toy-world camera, recognizable vehicles and pickups, readable driving surfaces and minimal obstruction.

families.label: Castle 3D
families.direction: Distinct island and castle silhouettes, tactile block edges, readable Crown protection and spatial impact feedback.

families.label: Live video core
families.direction: Real participant video is the stage; one prompt, a compact phase timer and unobtrusive readiness/voting controls.

games.name: Would You Rather
games.exception: Two equally legible options; keep the selected vote private until reveal and show majority/streak feedback afterward.

games.name: Doodle Guess
games.exception: Artist tools and guesser entry are role-specific; protect the canvas from chat, hints and the phone keyboard.

games.name: Truth or Dare
games.exception: Make the selected performer and Truth/Dare prompt the focus; show the room judgment as a later phase.

games.name: Never Have I Ever
games.exception: Have/Never must be equal, easy targets; response distribution should not replace the statement before voting ends.

games.name: Most Likely To
games.exception: A person-selection grid needs names and avatars, rather than answer cards; avoid hiding people below a tall prompt.

games.name: Hot Takes
games.exception: Distinguish take submission from Agree/Disagree voting; visualize divisiveness rather than suggesting majority approval wins.

games.name: Rank It
games.exception: Show all five positions and an explicit reorder affordance; submission state must not resemble a single-choice poll.

games.name: Two Truths & a Lie
games.exception: Keep all three statements comparable and anonymous during guessing; identify the lie only in the reveal.

games.name: Punchline
games.exception: Punchline needs a readable anonymous answer comparison and clear chosen-vote state; keep authors concealed until reveal.

games.name: Bluff
games.exception: Separate fake-answer entry from the mixed answer list; never visually privilege the real answer before reveal.

games.name: Story Builder
games.exception: Use a readable continuous story and obvious current author; avoid turning every sentence into a competing panel.

games.name: Emoji Story
games.exception: Let the emoji phrase be large and uncluttered; preserve a stable text guess input and keyboard clearance.

games.name: Trivia Blitz
games.exception: Four answer options still need full readable text; speed/streak feedback belongs after a confirmed answer.

games.name: Scattergories
games.exception: Category rows and the shared starting letter need stronger hierarchy than ornament; phone input must retain row context.

games.name: Word Chain
games.exception: Keep the previous word, living-player turn and challenge state explicit; rejected spellings remain editable on the same clock.

games.name: Word Countdown
games.exception: Nine letter tiles must show duplicate availability; Save, Lock in and Pass need distinct meanings and readable feedback.

games.name: Lyric Fill
games.exception: Show the lyric gap as the focal reading task; an editable answer line should not compete with decorative song imagery.

games.name: 5 Second Rule
games.exception: Name-three is a spoken social task; use a large category and unmistakable five-second phase, then separate judgment.

games.name: Charades
games.exception: Keep the secret acting word private to the performer; viewers need the live performer and a usable guess input.

games.name: 20 Questions
games.exception: Use a question transcript and remaining-question count; distinguish asking, answering and guessing from optional paid-score hints.

games.name: Pick One
games.exception: Two choices must remain reachable immediately for the five-second window; no elaborate entry transition.

games.name: Memory Tray
games.exception: Make the item arrangement memorable, then fully conceal it during recall; decoration must not accidentally supply answers.

games.name: Rapid Polls
games.exception: Custom questions and option lengths vary; let live results scale without destabilizing the voting controls.

games.name: Dare Roulette
games.exception: The spinner can be playful, but the landed dare and chicken action must be explicit and reachable.

games.name: Compliment Battle
games.exception: Give the target person a warm identity and the submitted text room to read; stage voting separately from composition.

games.name: Roast Toast
games.exception: Use the same target-and-answer clarity as Compliment Battle, with a distinct playful tone and readable gentle-roast prompt.

games.name: Draw Phone
games.exception: Writing, drawing and guessing need distinct tools; the final chain needs a readable ordered gallery rather than a single canvas.

games.name: Reaction Tap
games.exception: Red/wait and green/tap must also differ in text or shape; decoration must not look like the real start signal.

games.name: Typing Race
games.exception: The sentence, caret and correct/error progression are the playfield; allow keyboard space and keep the race meter secondary.

games.name: Number Hunt
games.exception: Numeric hotter/colder hints are not word similarity ranks; retain the guessed number and comparison direction in history.

games.name: Castle Clash
games.exception: Giggle has 2–4 individual Crowns and support-based block collapse; expose build/siege phases and own targeting without implying freeform physics or teams.

games.name: Chain Reaction
games.exception: This is turn-based 2–6-owner cellular capture, not falling-pair Puyo; show corner/edge/center capacity and gate input until settling finishes.

games.name: Checkers
games.exception: English compulsory captures and continued jumps need a legible selected piece/path; distinguish crowned kings from men without relying on color.

games.name: Chess
games.exception: Piece silhouettes, legal moves, promotion and optional clocks must remain readable; keep secondary room actions away from the board edge.

games.name: Fleet Duel
games.exception: Keep enemy ships hidden, including for spectators; show five-ship placement, chart coordinates, one-shot turns and the Aim/Fire confirmation distinctly.

games.name: Four in a Row
games.exception: The active target is a column rather than a cell; show gravity/drop direction and the winning four without equal-weight controls around every hole.

games.name: Kalah
games.exception: Use the actual six-bowl/four-seed preset, strong own-row/store ownership and clean counts; show sowing, capture and extra-turn feedback without chess-grid styling.

games.name: Ludo
games.exception: Four seats need distinct yard/home routes, active pawn choices, safe-square symbols and an obvious die action; preserve the shared Room launcher and short-screen reachability.

games.name: Pocket Karts
games.exception: Primary genre is free-driving kart combat: weapons, cover, knockouts, protected respawns and timed wins; no laps or finishing order. Use shared kart/weapon/pickup assets across maps. Elevations require real authoritative 3D physics, not decorative ramps.

games.name: Pose Party
games.exception: One performer is the hero; Ready precedes the peer Yes/No phase, and the prompt must not cover their body or face.

games.name: Reversi
games.exception: Use strong ivory/charcoal disc contrast, readable legal-placement dots and controlled flip sequencing; show automatic pass as a turn event.

games.name: Show & Go
games.exception: Everyone may show an object at once; use equitable video tiles and peer-only Yes votes, with readiness separate from voting.

games.name: Warm Words
games.exception: The key feedback is embedding similarity plus vocabulary rank, with lower rank closer and only rank 1 winning; use explicit rank/history and optional hint cost, not spelling-distance cues.

existingCritique.scope: Earlier Checkers/Kalah captures; root now owns the substantive art revision. This is baseline feedback, not final acceptance.
findings: Phone captures omit a clear game title; compact title plus active turn should establish identity.
Muted gray/olive full-screen gradients and repeated outlined cards flatten hierarchy; put coherent material detail on the board and quiet the chrome.
Charcoal checkers have weak slate-board separation and generic concentric bevel rings; strengthen silhouette/material, king marker and legal/selected cues.
Kalah count badges protrude below bowl rims and resemble instrumentation; integrate clear counts with the bowl surface and one lighting direction.
The roughly 190px-wide Kalah board wastes space in the 390px phone capture; increase useful board width and simplify vertical chrome.
Flip, Resign and Offer draw have the same large emphasis; group secondary actions compactly and make Help discoverable.
existingCritique.caveat: The phone fixture labels Room QA; it is not final shared-shell acceptance. The file named kalah-568x320.jpg is actually 568×419 full-page pixels, so 320px-high control reachability still requires native verification.
